glossary.definition: Powerful Trainer and Special Energy cards introduced in Black & White and reintroduced in Scarlet & Violet. A standard 60-card tournament deck is permitted strictly 1 ACE SPEC card in total.
glossary.example: Prime Catcher, Unfair Stamp, Secret Box, Hero's Cape, Sparkling Crystal.

glossary.definition: Highest-tier chase card rarity in the Scarlet & Violet era, featuring full-bleed custom artwork, unique textures, and card numbers exceeding the set's standard count.
glossary.example: Charizard ex SIR (Obsidian Flames #223), Greninja ex SIR (Twilight Masquerade #214).

glossary.definition: Japanese terminology equivalent to English Secret Illustration Rares (SIR) or Crown Zenith Galarian Gallery full arts with gold foil or distinctive textures.
glossary.example: Iono SAR (Clay Burst / Paldea Evolved), Mew ex SAR (Shiny Treasure ex / Paldean Fates).

glossary.definition: Single-star rarity cards in Scarlet & Violet featuring scenic, full-card illustrations of standard non-ex Pokémon (historically known as Art Rares or Character Rares).
glossary.example: Charmander IR (151 #168), Cleffa IR (Obsidian Flames #202), Magikarp IR (Paldea Evolved #203).

glossary.definition: Special reverse holographic foil pattern exclusive to Pokémon Card 151 and Prismatic Evolutions featuring repeated Master Ball stamps across the card background (1 per booster box in Japanese 151).
glossary.example: Gengar Masterball Holo, Pikachu Masterball Holo, Erika's Invitation Masterball Holo.

glossary.definition: Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) highest standard grade, indicating virtually perfect 55/45 to 60/40 centering, zero print lines, flawless corners, pristine edges, and untouched surface gloss.
glossary.example: A PSA 10 modern alternate art typically commands a 2.5x to 4.5x market premium over its raw Near Mint counterpart.

glossary.definition: Beckett Grading Services (BGS) holy grail certification awarded only when all four individual subgrades (Centering, Corners, Edges, Surface) receive a perfect 10.0 score.
glossary.example: BGS Black Label modern cards frequently trade for 5x to 15x standard PSA 10 values at major auction houses.

glossary.definition: A letter printed on the bottom-left corner of modern Pokémon cards (e.g., H, I, J) determining tournament format legality. Rotations periodically retire older letters from Standard format play.
glossary.example: Standard format in 2026 permits regulation marks H, I, and J (Mark G rotated out on Pokémon TCG Live March 26, 2026, and in-person Play! Pokémon events April 10, 2026).

glossary.definition: The official standardized plaintext formatting syntax used by Pokémon TCG Live and tournament organizers to import and export 60-card deck lists in one click.
glossary.relatedUrlLabel: Copy PTCGL String for Meta Decks

glossary.definition: Card condition standard showing minimal to no wear from handling, with clean borders, no whitening over 1mm, no creases, scratches, or surface indentations.
glossary.example: Baseline condition for raw single card pricing across TCGplayer and Cardmarket.

glossary.definition: A flagship collector product containing 9 booster packs (11 in special sets like 151 and Crown Zenith), exclusive foil promo card, card sleeves, dice, and energy cards.
glossary.example: Prismatic Evolutions ETB, 151 ETB with Snorlax Illustration Rare promo.

glossary.definition: An out-of-play game area distinct from the discard pile. Cards sent to the Lost Zone cannot be recovered by any card effects, powering mechanics like Comfey, Sableye, and Mirage Gate.
glossary.example: Lost Zone Box archetype, Giratina VSTAR Lost Impact.
